messages.author: Gustavo Seabra
messages.body:
Friends,
I'm looking for a tool that allows me to, starting from a PDB file with a double-strand DNA on it, mutate some nucleic acids but keeping the original backbone. Extra points if it can automatically apply the complementary mutations on the second strand.
Does anyone know of such a tool?
Thanks!
--
Gustavo Seabra

messages.author: Mariano Curti
messages.body:
Dear Gustavo,
Before the experts chime in: Have you considered PyMOL? There is a
function to perform mutations:
https://pymolwiki.org/index.php/Mutagenesis
It can also be quite easily turned into a python script, where you could
make sure the complementary mutations are performed as well.
Best,
Mariano

messages.author: Gustavo Seabra
messages.body:
Hi everyone,
Thanks a lot to everyone who answered, all suggestions were very good!
Just to give an update, Carlos's program has the advantage of automatically
handling a full sequence,while in Chimera (with `swapna`) I need to
do one-by-one. I don't know PyMol enough to have an opinion.
Thanks!
--
Gustavo Seabra.

messages.author: Vlad Cojocaru
messages.body:
Hi Gustavo,
I am glad you found a suitable solution !
Just for the record of this thread, I want to mention that around the
swapna function in Chimera a wrapper script can also be written to
process any DNA structure/sequence. We are using a self-written small
perl program that does exactly that ...
Cheers
Vlad
